title: Client-side wallet-connect DOM-XSS via spoofed EIP-6963 provider (docs/assets/wallet.js)
content: Comprehensive security review of the site's client-side code found two related, concrete DOM-XSS vulnerabilities in docs/assets/wallet.js, both stemming from the same trust boundary: the global `eip6963:announceProvider` window event, which ANY installed browser extension can dispatch (not just real wallets) to advertise a name/icon/uuid and a provider object. 1. `_openPopover()` interpolated `info.name`/`info.icon`/`info.uuid` directly into innerHTML with no escaping. A spoofed provider announcement with `info.icon = '">'` breaks out of the `src="..."` attribute and executes arbitrary JS in the page's own origin — this is a documented wallet-phishing risk class in the dapp ecosystem, not theoretical. 2. `_bind()` trusted whatever string a provider's own eth_requestAccounts call returned as the connected account, with zero format validation, before storing it in `this._account` — which then fans out unescaped into an aria-label, a Basescan href, and popover text across multiple call sites. A spoofed provider (same vector as #1) fully controls that string. Fix: added escapeHtml() (matching the existing pattern in report.js/hire.js/profile.js) for info.name/icon/uuid, and validated the account against /^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/ once at the point of entry (_bind() and the accountsChanged handler) rather than patching every downstream render site. Verified by dispatching a real spoofed CustomEvent with an XSS payload in headless Chromium and confirming no script execution, and by simulating a malformed-account provider and confirming the connection is refused. Shipped in PR #86.

title: CDP Bazaar 0/22 indexing matches an open, unresolved upstream issue (x402-foundation/x402#2112) — not VAPE's own declaration bug
content: Deep review of x402 Bazaar discovery/registration requirements, prompted by the persistent 0/22-27 offerings indexed result agents/cdp_bazaar_check.py has recorded since 2026-07-20 despite ongoing real settlements through CDP's facilitator. Confirmed by reading the actual @x402/extensions/bazaar SDK source (worker/node_modules) that VAPE's declared serviceName ("VAPE", 4 chars), per-route tags (3-4 entries, well under the SDK's MAX_TAGS=5/MAX_TAG_LEN=32), and iconUrl (a real https domain, not loopback/IP-literal) all pass sanitizeResourceServiceMetadata() validation cleanly — our own declaration is not silently dropped. Cross-referenced x402-foundation/x402#2112 (open, no maintainer resolution): a different, independently-implemented Cloudflare Worker + CDP facilitator + external-EOA-payout service, with confirmed real settlements, shows the identical symptom — CDP's facilitator never emits the documented EXTENSION-RESPONSES header confirming bazaar-extension acceptance/rejection, on either service. That reporter's own fix attempt (a Cloudflare Configuration Rule exempting Browser Integrity Check on paid routes, after finding non-browser User-Agents got 403'd) did NOT resolve their indexing either — the issue stayed open. An unconfirmed community hypothesis in the same thread (payTo may need to be a CDP-account-linked wallet, not an external EOA, for discovery indexing specifically, as opposed to permissionless settlement) has no support in CDP's docs or the x402 spec and is not being acted on without a maintainer confirmation. Added GET /admin/bazaar-validate (worker/src/index.ts) as a live, honest probe of CDP's documented POST /v2/x402/validate diagnostic, reusing the exact manual-JWT auth already proven correct by /admin/bazaar-status — returns CDP's raw response verbatim since no verified exact response schema could be obtained (the CDP docs page itself blocks automated fetchers). Also found and left in place (currently dead code, not a live bug): worker/src/index.ts's buildCreateAuthHeaders() has no "bazaar" key, so the SDK's own withBazaar(cdpClient).extensions.bazaar helper would send an unauthenticated request if anything ever called it — nothing does today (both admin endpoints build their own JWT manually instead), so this doesn't affect current behavior, but would need a fix if that helper is ever wired up directly.
